newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends strong on funds, soyoil falters.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends strong on funds, soyoil falters.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed higher on Wednesday amid heavy fund buying with talk of export business lending fundemental support, traders said.
Soyoil futures again faltered as traders pointed to a bearish fundamental outlook. Funds and commission houses were sellers on the day.
"Funds were big buyers in meal and beans, something like 3,000 meal was bought and nine million in beans," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Prudential Securities bought 600 lots March soymeal and 100 lots December, traders said.
LIT America, Refco Inc, Smith Barney, Tenco Inc and Dean Witter each bought 300 lots March and Merrill Lynch bought 400 March, they said.
Soyoil continued to look fundementally weak. High crushing rates were producing massive soyoil stockpiles with little demand in sight, traders noted.
"They're crushing for meal and oil is just what's left over," one trader said.
Soymeal ended $3.50 to $1.50 per ton higher with March up $3.50 at $240.40. Soyoil closed 0.05 to 0.02 per lb lower with March down 0.05 at 24.11 cents.
On the day, Cargill Inc sold 300 lots March soyoil and 50 lots May. Griffin Trading sold 250 lots March and Smith Barney sold 200 March, traders said.

Soymeal volume was estimated at 15,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 10,709 lots, according to CBOT. Soyoil volume was pegged at 10,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 10,644 lots, CBOT reported.
